events.text: The clouds under your isle stop moving. All of them, to the horizon, as if a hand had been laid flat on the sky. The cloud-barge pilots at your landing take off their hats without being told why. An old Ministry clerk walking the White Stairs says only: "It is looking at you," and does not wait for an answer.

choices.text: Face the sky, and bow low

effects.log: You bow. The clouds stay still a while longer, and then, politely, begin to drift again.

choices.text: Look straight back at the sky

effects.log: You look back. Nothing happens, and that nothing has weight.

choices.text: Ask the Ministry clerk what they have seen before

effects.log: The clerk tells you three stories, and each ends with a name nobody says aloud. You listen to all of them.

events.text: A single lantern appears on your windowsill at the hour of the rat, lit with white fire that gives no heat. In the morning the spirit-beasts of your isle will not cross your threshold. A Court astrologer leans out of a passing barge and calls down, rather too cheerfully, that your star has been moved on the chart.

choices.text: Set an offering beside the lantern

effects.log: You set out rice wine and a sprig of pine. By dawn the lantern is gone and the cup is empty.

choices.text: Snuff the white flame between two fingers

effects.log: It goes out. Your fingers will not warm for a week, and you are strangely glad.

choices.text: Copy the Court astrologer's new chart

effects.log: You copy it with care. Your star has been moved, but toward what the chart does not say.

events.text: Your first dream in a century is of a great eye, patient and dry, resting on the White Stairs where you once climbed. You wake with the taste of rain on a clear day. Three of your neighbours on the isle report the same dream, and none of them, they insist, have done anything at all.

choices.text: Burn incense at the Dao Shrine on your isle

effects.log: The smoke rises straight as a rule. You take it for an answer, or for politeness.

choices.text: Tell no one, and cultivate through the night

effects.log: You sit until the stars turn. Whatever was looking waits, and you do not break first.

choices.text: Compare the dreams with your neighbours, in detail

effects.log: Between you, you assemble the eye very exactly. It is not comforting. It is, however, accurate.

events.text: A crack of thunder out of a blue noon, one clap, directly over your roof. The slates do not move. The tea in your cup trembles into a perfect ring. Down at the Palace of the Nine Clouds a bell that has not rung for ninety years begins, shyly, to hum.

choices.text: Kneel on the roof tiles until the hum stops

effects.log: You kneel. The hum fades after the third breath, as a guest might quietly leave.

choices.text: Stand in the thunder's place and hold your ground

effects.log: You stand where the sound fell. Your hair rises, your knees do not bend, and the sky takes note.

choices.text: Take the trembling tea to an old tribulation-warden

effects.log: The warden reads the ring in the cup and names a date. You write the date down. It is a good many years off.

events.text: It is no longer only watching. The lightning that crosses your isle at noon has begun to stop on your threshold, and wait. Cloud-barge captains steer wide. The Jade Court's Ministry of Tribulations sends a polite note, three lines long, asking whether you have thought of taking a long journey. It does not say it is an order.

choices.text: Pay the Ministry's fee and ask for a warding

effects.log: The warding is expensive and pretty. Whether it works, nobody will say for certain, and that is also an answer.

choices.text: Walk out into the waiting lightning

effects.log: You walk into it. It parts around you the way a crowd parts for a stranger it has not decided about.

choices.text: Take the long journey, and see who follows

effects.log: You go, quietly, by the lower stair. Something does follow, at a courteous distance, and keeps your pace.

events.text: Your cultivation hall has grown a draught. It comes from nowhere, smells of cold metal, and turns the pages of your books to the same passage every time: a line about those whom the Dao permits to rise, and the price it asks. Your disciples refuse to sit in the east corner. One of them weeps and cannot say why.

choices.text: Read the passage aloud, in full, with respect

effects.log: You read it. The draught stops mid-page and lies down like a dog that has been spoken to.

choices.text: Wedge the book shut and cultivate in the draught

effects.log: You do. It is the coldest meditation of your life, and you come out of it sharper.

choices.text: Ask a Cloud Library scribe who else has had this

effects.log: The scribe finds you four names, two erased and two ascended. You are shown which were which.

events.text: A herald of the Jade Court stands on your landing with a scroll and no seal. "Not an order," it says, in a voice with nothing behind it. "An observation." The scroll lists, with admirable neutrality, every place you have stepped in the last forty years. At the bottom is one line left blank, for you to fill in.

choices.text: Fill the line in with your own name and rank

effects.log: The ink dries at once. The herald nods, takes the scroll, and does not look at you again.

choices.text: Leave the line blank, and hand the scroll back

effects.log: The herald holds it a moment, as if weighing a blank. Then it goes, and does not argue.

choices.text: Write a question on the line instead

effects.log: You write: "Why?" The herald reads it, folds the scroll very small, and promises nothing.

events.text: The stars over your isle are wrong in a small, precise way: nine of them have stepped half a finger to the left. Astrologers across the Celestial Ministries argue by lamplight about whether to tell you. They decide they must, and send a young one, who stands in your doorway with her hands shaking and says: "It is aimed at you."

choices.text: Thank the young astrologer, and send her home safely

effects.log: She goes home on your own barge, with an escort. It is a small, steadying kindness, and the sky seems to note it.

choices.text: Ask her to draw the aim line, and walk along it

effects.log: The line runs out to the edge of the cloud-sea. You stand at the end of it, and feel the other end.

choices.text: Offer her a place on your isle for as long as it lasts

effects.log: She stays. Her charts become a good deal better, and so does your hall's mood.

events.text: Heaven has taken a side, and it will not say which. The tribulation clouds above your isle part to show a clear lane of sky, like a road. The lightning draws back from the lane's edge in two straight lines. Somewhere beyond the Jade Court a very old voice says your name once, quite kindly, and you cannot tell whether it is a blessing or a sentence.

choices.text: Walk the cleared lane with bowed head

effects.log: You walk it. Nothing strikes you. Nothing welcomes you either. The lane simply ends, a long way on.

choices.text: Step off the lane, and climb by your own road

effects.log: You step off. The lightning closes in behind, and the sky is quiet in a way that feels like waiting.

choices.text: Stay where you are, and learn what the lane is for

effects.log: You watch it for three nights. It is not for you. It is for what comes after you, and that is worse.

events.text: The White Stairs have grown a seventy-first step, overnight, where none existed. It is plain white, and faintly warm, and it ends in thin air a handspan above the cloud-sea. A queue of the very old gathers to look. None of them step on it. One of them says it was built for you, and that she was there when the last one was.

choices.text: Set one foot on the step, as a guest might

effects.log: The step holds. It is warm, and it hums, and you step back down having been seen.

choices.text: Refuse the step, and build your own stairs

effects.log: You order a stair carved on your own isle. It is crooked and ugly and yours, and heaven watches it being built.

choices.text: Ask the old ones what became of the last who climbed it

effects.log: Three of them tell you three different endings. Between the three there is a hole exactly your size.

events.text: The Jade Court's Archivist comes in person, which she has not done in four hundred years, and sits in your hall without being asked. "Heaven's ledger has you on two pages," she says. "One is for those it means to raise. The other is for those it means to correct. I do not know which will turn first." She drinks your tea. It is very quiet.

choices.text: Ask the Archivist how a person might deserve the first page

effects.log: She tells you, honestly, in six sentences. You write them down and do not enjoy them.

choices.text: Tell the Archivist you will not be on either page

effects.log: She smiles for the first time in four hundred years. "Then you will be a third thing. Good luck."

choices.text: Ask to read the second page, and see what it says

effects.log: She shows you. It names no crime. It names only your pace, and a date, and nothing else.

events.text: Every immortal on your isle wakes at the same moment, hair standing on end, saying the same two words in their sleep. It takes a day to learn what they were. They were your name, in the old tongue, followed by a rest. Not a full stop. A rest, as in music: a note of silence that waits for what comes next.

choices.text: Sit with your people and share the silence

effects.log: You sit till dawn. Nobody speaks. By morning something in the air has chosen, and it chose gently.

choices.text: Break the silence, aloud, with your own name

effects.log: You say it, loudly, in the common tongue. The rest ends. Whatever it was waiting for, you have given it something else.

choices.text: Write down the two words and bury them under the isle

effects.log: You bury them under the hearthstone. The isle grows a little steadier, a little heavier, a little yours.

events.text: The Heavenly Dao has rewritten your destiny, and left the ink wet. A Court scribe comes to your door with the new page and cannot meet your eye. {hv9_fate}, it says, in a hand not human. Spirit-beasts on the isle bow low as you pass. A rival's cloud-barge turns around halfway to your landing. You have not done anything yet. It is only that you are expected to.

choices.text: Read the page aloud, and let your isle hear it

effects.log: You read it. Your isle goes quiet, then, one by one, starts to stand up straighter.

choices.text: Accept the title and tell no one

effects.log: You fold the page away. The weight is a pleasure at first and a tax by the end of the week.

choices.text: Tear the page in two and sit on the pieces

effects.log: It does not matter. It is already true. But your hands shake less afterward.

events.text: A column of pale light stands on the White Stairs at noon, and you are the only one it casts a shadow for. The Ministry of Rites sends robes the colour of new snow. The page reads: {hv9_fate}. Elder immortals bow to you in the corridor; younger ones watch you with an expression you remember from your own youth, directed at someone else.

choices.text: Wear the white robes and go to the Court

effects.log: You wear them. The Court receives you with a courtesy that is a little too well rehearsed.

choices.text: Give the robes to a disciple, and wear your old ones

effects.log: The disciple wears them badly. The Court takes note that you are not easily dressed.

choices.text: Ask what is expected of the chosen, in plain words

effects.log: The answer is brief and sobering. You write it above your door.

events.text: Your name has been struck from the Jade Court's Roll of Orthodoxy, and a new line has appeared in a darker hand: {hv9_fate}. No one has accused you of anything. The Demon Realm sends a cordial, unsigned invitation. A Ministry inspector arrives the same afternoon and says, with great delicacy, that he has not seen you today.

choices.text: Show the inspector your hall, and keep nothing back

effects.log: He goes through it twice and writes very little. He is relieved, and so, you find, are you.

choices.text: Answer the Demon Realm's invitation with a polite, empty cup

effects.log: The cup is returned full. It is a message, but you are not yet sure of the language.

choices.text: Visit the oldest immortal on your isle and ask what the page really means

effects.log: The old immortal laughs, then does not. The advice that follows is long and kind.

events.text: The lamps of the Nine Clouds Palace gutter as you pass, and the elders watch from behind pillars. The new page names you {hv9_fate}, and below it, in a smaller hand, a note that you will, with time, be very good at what you are about to do. The cloud-barge captains charge you double. The tea-seller on the lower landing gives you a cup for free.

choices.text: Take the page to the Palace and read it before the elders

effects.log: They hear it in silence. Then they argue, and you listen, and it teaches you a great deal.

choices.text: Befriend the tea-seller, who is the only honest voice left

effects.log: She tells you her family's own story of the dark road. It is humane, and also, quite practical.

choices.text: Spend the year making sure nobody follows you onto this road

effects.log: You work hard at being unfollowable. It is lonely, and it works.

events.text: A comet crosses the afternoon sky, tail the colour of old bronze, and the Ministry of Stars strikes your name in red. {hv9_fate}, says the page, and under it a warning that nobody on the isles can quite agree how to read. Cloud-barges hang back from your landing. Your disciples lie awake. The old tea-seller says that bright things get looked at, and sometimes broken.

choices.text: Stand under the comet and let the isles see you

effects.log: You stand there an hour. Whatever is looking, the isles are looking too, and you find you can bear that.

choices.text: Close your gates for a season, and let the comet pass

effects.log: It passes. The red name remains on the chart, a little fainter, and your hall has had a rest.

choices.text: Send your disciples away to safer isles

effects.log: They resist. They go. Your hall is empty and quiet, and you are very sure of yourself.

events.text: It is written in the Book of Stars in letters that smoke: {hv9_fate}. Where you walk, glass cracks along the paths. The wind changes direction around your isle. Nothing terrible has happened, and the clerks of the Ministry of Stars still draw back from you as if something might. The Archivist says it may mean nothing at all. She says it very firmly.

choices.text: Read the entry to the Ministry, and ask them to correct it

effects.log: They cannot. They can, however, add a footnote, and the footnote is kinder than the entry.

choices.text: Walk in the open on purpose, to show nothing breaks

effects.log: Nothing breaks, for a month. The isle watches, and some part of it learns to breathe.

choices.text: Go down to the cloud-sea and sit by it for a year

effects.log: It is a good year. Whatever the page means, it did not happen there.

events.text: An old life is stirring under your new one. The Heavenly Dao rewrites your page, and on it the name {hv9_fate}, and a line of text you do not recognise but remember. Your dreams are suddenly full of a road you walked a long time ago, and a door you have already closed. Old rivals, very old ones, ask after you in the tea-houses, politely, by your former name.

choices.text: Say the old name aloud, and let it settle

effects.log: You say it. The air in your hall sounds like a held breath, then a long one let go.

choices.text: Go looking for the first door you closed

effects.log: You find it, and it is smaller than you remembered. You do not open it. You are glad to have seen it.

choices.text: Write the old life down, all of it, in plain prose

effects.log: It takes a winter. The book is slim and honest. You put it in the Cloud Library under an invented name.

events.text: The Court's Archivist brings you a cup of old tea and a single sheet. {hv9_fate}, it reads, in a hand you swear you have seen before. "This is the second time heaven has written you," she says. "It does not usually correct the same person twice. I am not sure it knows what to do with you." She seems almost pleased about it.

choices.text: Ask the Archivist what heaven wrote the first time

effects.log: She tells you, as far as she can read it. The first life and the second look like each other, quietly.

choices.text: Pour the wine on the White Stairs for the one you were

effects.log: The stone drinks it. A faint warmth runs up the steps and is gone.

choices.text: Ask what heaven means to do with someone it cannot finish

effects.log: She has no answer, and says so. You are oddly grateful for that.

events.text: Prayer to you goes silent for the length of a breath, in every temple at once. Your heralds stop in the star-road as if they had walked into glass. Then the prayer comes back, a little changed, with something underneath it that is not faith. The Book of Fates, which you have never had to consult, lies open on your altar to a page you did not turn.

choices.text: Close the Book gently, and give it a place of honour

effects.log: You close it, set it on a clean cloth, and put a lamp beside it. The lamp burns very straight.

choices.text: Leave the Book open, and read the page standing

effects.log: You read it standing. It contains one sentence, about you, and you read it again, and then you leave it open.

choices.text: Ask your oldest herald what the silence was

effects.log: The herald thinks for a long time. "Attention," it says. "The kind with no face."

events.text: The star-road under your temple has gone dim in one stretch, as if a great shadow had paused over it. Pilgrims on that stretch walk in silence. Your lesser gods report the same: a weight on the sky above their domains, like a hand deciding whether to press. For a thousand years you have been the one who watches. It is odd to be watched.

choices.text: Light the first lamp on the star-road, and keep it

effects.log: You light it. The shadow passes slowly, not leaving, but no longer pressing.

choices.text: Walk out into the dim and meet whatever is above

effects.log: You walk out. The star-road holds, and the weight, for a time, does not come down.

choices.text: Gather your lesser gods for a council in the open

effects.log: They come, shy and curious. You learn who has been watched, and who has only been afraid.

events.text: Your offerings come back. Every one of them, the incense, the grain, the thousand-year wine, set neatly on your altar by invisible hands. Your faithful weep and your lesser gods whisper. It is not a rejection. It is, you realise slowly, a message: the Dao has no use for what you were giving it, and wants something else.

choices.text: Offer nothing at all, and sit in the quiet

effects.log: You sit. The offerings fade from the altar one by one, as dew does, with no ceremony.

choices.text: Offer your own name, written small, on a paper boat

effects.log: You set the boat on the river of the star-road. It goes on a long time without sinking.

choices.text: Ask the faithful what they think the Dao wants

effects.log: Their answers are modest and astonishingly sharp. You write down three and keep them.

events.text: A herald from the Hall of Lesser Heavens delivers a letter that is not from any god. It is blank except for your name in a script you recognise from before the pantheons, and a mark like a closed eyelid. Your herald trembles, then laughs, then cries. "I have never carried one," she says. "They say it comes once, and only to those it means to see."

choices.text: Hold the blank letter to your heart and say thanks

effects.log: The letter warms and goes still. You are not sure what you thanked, only that it heard.

choices.text: Write your own reply on the blank page

effects.log: You write: "I am here." The ink sinks into the paper, and the paper into the air.

choices.text: Keep the letter and tell no one for a century

effects.log: You keep it in a plain box. It is heavier each decade, and you are used to that.

events.text: It is no longer only watching. Your domain is being edited. A river of your faithful runs a little to the left, a mountain folds half a league east, a festival day shifts a week. Nothing is wrong, exactly. Everything is simply being adjusted, with gentle, unhurried care, by a hand that does not trouble itself to ask you first.

choices.text: Accept the adjustments, and bless the new river

effects.log: You bless it. It runs more smoothly for your blessing, and the faithful believe it was always so.

choices.text: Move the river back with your own divine hand

effects.log: You move it. It resists, slightly, like a person who has been told to sit down. Then it yields, and the sky takes note.

choices.text: Ask the Archivist of the Book of Fates what is being corrected

effects.log: She is delighted to be asked. She talks for a day. The thread of it is: you, and a pattern the Dao dislikes.

events.text: The heralds of the Dao have never been seen. Tonight, one of them is: a pale, patient figure at the foot of your altar, hands folded. It does not speak. It looks at your offerings, then at your faithful, then at you, and writes something with a finger on the air, which you can read, and wish you could not. Then it goes, leaving the altar cold.

choices.text: Read what it wrote aloud, and answer it

effects.log: You answer: "Yes." The air agrees, in a way that costs you something and gives something back.

choices.text: Wipe the air clean with your sleeve

effects.log: You wipe it. The words stay behind your eyelids. It was not a thing that could be wiped.

choices.text: Search the Book of Fates for the herald's name

effects.log: The Book has no such page. It has instead a thick, careful blank that reads like a held breath.

events.text: Your prayers have developed an echo. Whatever a pilgrim asks of you, a half-beat later the same words return from above, spoken more slowly. The faithful think it a miracle. Your lesser gods think it an audit. You have begun to answer with great care, as one speaks in a room where the walls are listening.

choices.text: Answer every prayer with courtesy and plain truth

effects.log: You do. The echo grows quiet and wondering, as though a listener had set down a pen.

choices.text: Pray back, loud and long, to whatever listens

effects.log: You pray: "What do you want?" The echo repeats it. Then, for one breath, does not.

choices.text: Take the prayers to a quiet hill and listen with no words

effects.log: It takes ten years. You come down with a slightly different face and a better ear.

events.text: A wind blows through the Hall of Lesser Heavens in which no flame moves. Gods of three pantheons bow their heads in turn, as it passes. When it reaches you, it stops. It is neither warm nor cold. It reads you like a page, line by line, and you let it, because the alternative is a game you have not been taught.

choices.text: Hold still and let the wind finish its reading

effects.log: It finishes. It lifts your hair once, and goes on. You are not unmade. You are, on the whole, noted.

choices.text: Speak into the wind and make it answer

effects.log: You speak. It answers in one syllable, far too large for the room, and then the room is quiet and wholly yours.

choices.text: Study the pattern the wind leaves on the Hall's floor

effects.log: It is a spiral, and in the spiral is a gap. You mark where the gap sits.

events.text: The Dao has taken a side, and it will not say which. The Book of Fates closes itself on your altar with a sound like a door in a distant house. Star-roads shift. Lesser gods stop mid-sentence, to listen to a voice only they can hear. Then, from everywhere, a single quiet word in the old speech. It might be your name. It might be a verdict.

choices.text: Go to your temple's highest roof and bow to the whole sky

effects.log: You bow. The sky does nothing, grandly. After a long while, you straighten up.

choices.text: Speak to the Dao as an equal, once, and plainly

effects.log: You speak. It does not answer. It does not need to. The silence has gained a listener.

choices.text: Gather your faithful and tell them the truth, as you know it

effects.log: You tell them: you do not know. They stay. It is the most honest thing you have ever said from an altar.

events.text: A second sun rises over your temple, small and pale. It casts no shadows. The faithful crowd the courtyard, awestruck, but your heralds hold them back. They understand what you understand: the sun is not a gift, it is an eye. It has found the thing it was looking for. It has not yet decided what to do with you.

choices.text: Walk out under the pale sun and give it your open hands

effects.log: You do. It stays above you for nine breaths, then rises, content, or at least unconcerned.

choices.text: Raise your own light against it, and hold it there

effects.log: Your light is a candle against the sky. It holds. The pale sun narrows, interested.

choices.text: Order the courtyard emptied, and watch alone

effects.log: The courtyard empties. You watch alone, and whatever happens, it happens to you only.

events.text: The Archivist of the Book of Fates arrives at your temple at dusk, on foot, which no Archivist has done in an age. "Two ledgers," she says, without greeting. "One for those the Dao raises. One for those it prunes. Your page is in both, and I swear I did not write it." She puts down a lamp, and you see her hands tremble.

choices.text: Ask the Archivist to sit, and offer her a cup

effects.log: She sits. She says nothing for a long time. It is the kindest silence you have had in centuries.

choices.text: Tell the Archivist you will write your own page

effects.log: She stares at you. Then, very quietly, she hands you a pen. It is just an ordinary pen.

choices.text: Ask which page is the older one

effects.log: The pruning page is older. That tells you something about what the Dao has been waiting for.

events.text: All your lesser gods wake in the same instant and kneel, facing a direction in which there is no wall. They are not praying. They are, you realise, listening to something that is addressed to you through them. It is slow, vast and patient. Its tone is that of a great judge reading a long case, and finding it of interest.

choices.text: Kneel with them and listen to the end

effects.log: You listen. It does not end. It only gets quieter, until you cannot tell it from your own pulse.

choices.text: Stand, and ask it to speak to you directly

effects.log: You stand. A silence follows that is not refusal. It feels like a door left ajar.

choices.text: Record every word the gods repeat, and weigh them

effects.log: You write for a night. In the morning you have a page, and the page is almost a sentence.

events.text: The Dao has rewritten your destiny and left the Book of Fates open. {hv9_fate}, it reads, on your own page, in a hand no god has ever claimed. Your heralds come to look and do not speak. Your faithful feel it as warmth on the back of the neck. Domains of rival gods lean toward you, the way plants turn to light, whether or not they would like to.

choices.text: Proclaim the new destiny to your temples

effects.log: You proclaim it. Faith rises like a tide, and for a short, sweet while you let it carry you.

choices.text: Keep the page closed, and live as though it had not changed

effects.log: You try. The world around you rearranges itself to fit, and you learn how loud quiet can be.

choices.text: Ask your oldest herald what it feels like from outside

effects.log: The herald is honest: like standing near a great fire that has decided to like you.

events.text: A hymn you did not write is sung in your temples tonight, in a dozen tongues, the same tune everywhere. {hv9_fate}, runs the refrain. Lesser gods, long wary, offer you the first cup at their feasts. A rival pantheon sends a delegation with gifts. The Dao has chosen. It does not say for what, and not knowing is a weight of its own.

choices.text: Accept the first cup and speak of it plainly

effects.log: You say: the Dao has chosen, and I do not know why. It is the right thing to say, and they remember it.

choices.text: Refuse the gifts and keep your temples humble

effects.log: The gifts go home, bewildered. Your faithful nod, approving, and your altar grows warm.

choices.text: Spend a century in the Hall of Fates reading how it ends

effects.log: It does not end. It goes on, in a script too long to read, and you leave knowing it is not finished.

events.text: Your page in the Book has gone dark, edges singed. The Dao writes {hv9_fate}, there, in ink the colour of a bruise. No god has said a word against you. But the heralds of three pantheons now take the long way round your temples, and your faithful, at night, lower their voices when they pray. There is a hunger in the title, and it is yours.

choices.text: Read the entry before your assembled faithful and tell them its meaning

effects.log: They hear it. Some leave. Most stay, and a few, oddly, grow braver.

choices.text: Seek out a god of the old dark roads, and ask for counsel

effects.log: The old god is courteous and very tired. The counsel is practical, and unexpectedly kind.

choices.text: Quiet your temples and fast for a season

effects.log: The hunger in the page does not go. But you hold it, and holding it is a kind of freedom.

events.text: The Dao's new entry for you is short: {hv9_fate}. Its heralds do not speak it aloud. Offerings at your altar change; the grain is blacker, the wine less sweet, the prayers more urgent and less polite. Your lesser gods are uneasy, and some are leaving. But the ones who stay say, quietly, that they would rather be near a power that knows its own mind.

choices.text: Thank the ones who stay, by name, one by one

effects.log: You do. It takes nine days. It is the longest litany of your life, and a good one.

choices.text: Make a rule for your temples: no prayer may be forced

effects.log: The rule holds. The dark offerings keep coming, but they come freely, which is something.

choices.text: Climb to the edge of your domain and look at what is beyond

effects.log: Beyond is a country you have not governed. It is wide. You mark it on your map.

events.text: A star in your domain's sky dims, burns white, and goes out. The Book of Fates rewrites you as {hv9_fate}, with a clerk's note in the margin: "Handle with great care." Your heralds ask, in carefully level voices, whether the temple should be moved. Your faithful say it is a great honour. Their eyes say otherwise. The Dao is not cruel. It simply does not look away.

choices.text: Stand the temple's ground, and tell the pilgrims plainly what it means

effects.log: You tell them. A few go home. The rest settle in for a long vigil, and you are glad of the company.

choices.text: Invite a rival god to share your watch

effects.log: The rival comes, astonished and grave. You find you are no longer entirely alone in it.

choices.text: Move the whole temple to a quiet valley, for a quiet age

effects.log: The valley is lovely. Whatever the star was, it has not followed, yet.

events.text: Storms gather at the borders of your domain and then, as if embarrassed, do not cross. The Book of Fates names you {hv9_fate}, and gives no reason. A lesser god begs you to leave their mountain. Another offers you a whole range, as a gift, to keep your trouble away from theirs. You have done nothing yet. It is only that the world listens for what you will do.

choices.text: Accept the gift range and go there for a decade

effects.log: It is a fine range, empty and clean. In ten years you learn to be a calamity that sits quite still.

choices.text: Stay, and ask the begging god what they fear

effects.log: They tell you. It is small and human, and you promise to be careful of it.

choices.text: Write a vow in the Book, in your own hand, beneath the entry

effects.log: The vow is accepted, or at least not struck out. It sits beneath the title, small and stubborn.

events.text: The Dao has found you again. {hv9_fate}, it writes, and under it, in an older hand still, a title you used to hold in a time before this pantheon. Heralds of an extinct court appear at your gates, fresh and bewildered, bowing to you by your first name. The Book of Fates is open to a page ten thousand years older than the one you were reading.

choices.text: Welcome the old heralds, and let them tell what they remember

effects.log: They tell it. It is a long account, and much of it is yours, and you listen as if to a stranger.

choices.text: Close the old page and keep only the new

effects.log: You close it. The old page does not mind. It has been closed before, and it knows how to wait.

choices.text: Name the extinct court's hall and hold a feast in its honour

effects.log: The hall is vacant, but the feast is full. For one night, the dead courtesies are alive.

events.text: In the deepest vault of the Hall of Fates, the Archivist lifts a lid you did not know existed, and shows you a page already written: {hv9_fate}. It has your handwriting on it. It is dated before you were born, and again after. "The Dao has never had to rewrite a god from their own draft," she says. "Do you mind terribly if I stay and watch?"

choices.text: Invite the Archivist to stay, and begin reading the draft together

effects.log: You read for a week. The draft is plain, hopeful, and unfinished. The Archivist cries a little, and so do you.

choices.text: Thank her, and ask for the page to be sealed

effects.log: She seals it. The seal is her own. It is a kindness, and it is a trust.

choices.text: Rewrite the last line of the draft yourself

effects.log: You do. It is only one line. The Archivist holds the lamp steady and does not look away.
